transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in. What brings you here today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my wife thinks I'm not eating enough. She's been worrying a bit. But honestly, most days I just have some coffee and a piece of toast in the morning. Then later on, maybe a little soup or some vegetables. Big meals just feel unnecessary to me at my age. I don't see the need for them.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticing that you don't enjoy things the way you used to?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I feel alright. I'm not sad or down, and I still enjoy doing my usual things around the house. My mood is perfectly fine, really. It's just the meals that my wife is worried about.
Have you or your wife noticed any recent problems with your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations or events?

No, I don't think so. My memory seems as sharp as it's always been. My wife hasn't mentioned anything about me forgetting things, either. I remember our conversations and what's going on day to day just fine.
Are you trying to limit how much you eat because you're worried about gaining weight or how your body looks?

Well, yes, I suppose I am. I mean, when my wife tries to put butter on things or serves me a full plate, I just... I get nervous. I don't want to start putting weight back on. I've worked hard to keep my weight down and stay in control of it, and eating all that just feels like I'd be losing that control. So I prefer to keep things light.
When you look at yourself now, how would you describe your current body weight or shape—do you feel you are still too heavy, or would you say you're thin or underweight?

I wouldn't say I'm thin or underweight, no. I just... well, I pay attention to how things fit and how I look. If my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It means I'm keeping on track. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, I feel sloppy and disappointed. So I don't see myself as too thin at all, I just want to make sure I don't get heavy.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and whether your weight has changed significantly over the past several months?

Well, I'm about five foot nine. As for my weight, yes, it has gone down over the past several months. My regular doctor actually tells me the number on the scale has gotten too low. But honestly, I don't see it as a problem. To me, being lighter just makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up on my walks.
